rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earth is a visible thing, whereas sky names what is elevated and shades; the terms do not simply denote opposite directions.
rows.anchor: السماء أطلقت على كل ما علا فأظل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause is a true exclusivity addressed to idolaters who knew God created but acted as though ignorant through shirk and neglect of worship and gratitude.
rows.anchor: صيغة قصر وهو قصر حقيقي سيق للمخاطبين من المشركين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reminder identifies God as creator of earth, its surface, and its interior, and says all this was created for human benefit across changing times and circumstances.
rows.anchor: التذكير بأن الله هو خالق الأرض وما عليها وما في داخلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author compares the reminder with the claim that creator and noncreator are unlike and that idols cannot create even a fly; idolaters treated idols as intercessors, not creators.
rows.anchor: ما كانوا يثبتون لأصنامهم قدرة على الخلق وإنما جعلوها شفعاء ووسائط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The compact insertion of for you replaces a full explanation and displays divine power, favor, humanity's standing, and a reason to uproot disbelief.
rows.anchor: والمقصود من الكلام فيما أراه موافقا للبلاغة التذكير بأن الله هو خالق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The purposive lām raises whether divine acts have ends; Muslims agree acts follow divine will, choice, and knowledge and contain wisdoms and benefits, while dispute concerns calling these aims or final causes.
rows.anchor: المسألة مختلف فيها بين المتكلمين اختلافا يشبه أن يكون لفظيا

rows.speaker: جماعة المثبتين
rows.claim: A group affirms purposes in divine acts, adducing verses such as God's creation of jinn and humans to worship Him.
rows.anchor: فأثبت ذلك جماعة استدلالا بما

rows.speaker: أصحاب الأشعري
rows.claim: As Fakhr reports their view, Ashʿarī followers deny divine acts have purposes: an agent who acts for a purpose would benefit from it and need the cause.
rows.anchor: ومنع من ذلك أصحاب الأشعري

rows.speaker: جمهور الفقهاء والمتكلمين
rows.claim: Al-Shāṭibī reports that most jurists and theologians regard God's rulings as grounded in interests and prevention of harms.
rows.anchor: عن جمهور الفقهاء والمتكلمين أن أحكام الله تعالى معللة بالمصالح ودرء المفاسد

rows.speaker: ابن عرفة
rows.claim: Ibn ʿArafa distinguishes the disputed grounding of God's acts from His rulings, which he says are grounded in interests.
rows.anchor: هذا هو تعليل أفعال الله تعالى وفيه خلاف وأما أحكامه فمعللة

rows.speaker: الرازي والبيضاوي وصاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī, al-Bayḍāwī, al-Zamakhsharī, some Muʿtazilites and Shāfiʿī and Ḥanafī authorities infer that using things is originally permitted; the view is also attributed to al-Shāfiʿī.
rows.anchor: الإمام الرازي والبيضاوي وصاحب ( الكشاف )

rows.speaker: المالكية وجمهور الحنفية
rows.claim: Mālikīs and most Ḥanafīs, along with the Muʿtazilites in Ibn ʿArafa's report, hold that the original status of things is suspension and reject the verse as proof.
rows.anchor: وذهب المالكية وجمهور الحنفية والمعتزلة في نقل ابن عرفة إلى أن الأصل في الأشياء الوقف

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: Ibn al-ʿArabī reads the verse as evidence of God's power, knowledge, ordering, and direction of created things, not as a rule of permissibility.
rows.anchor: قال ابن العربي في ( أحكامه )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse is general and intended to alert people to the Creator's power; creation for humanity does not make every possible use lawful, and the verse addresses disbelievers rather than legislating for them.
rows.anchor: والحق أن الآية مجملة قصد منها التنبيه على قدرة الخالق بخلق ما في الأرض وأنه خلق لأجلنا إلا أن خلقه لأجلنا لا يستلزم إباحة استعماله في كل ما يقصد منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The grant is for humanity collectively: the whole created domain belongs to people as a whole, not every item to every individual, as al-Bayḍāwī observes.
rows.anchor: أن الآية ذكرت أن المجموع للمجموع لا كل واحد لكل واحد كما أشار إليه البيضاوي

rows.speaker: بعض أهل الحديث وبعض المعتزلة
rows.claim: Some hadith scholars and some Muʿtazilites hold that things are originally forbidden; al-Qurṭubī notes that Muʿtazilites are reported to hold all three positions.
rows.anchor: وذهب جماعة إلى أن أصل الأشياء الحظر ونقل عن بعض أهل الحديث وبعض المعتزلة

rows.speaker: الإمام الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī says the dispute matters especially for acts during the pre-prophetic interval and regards suspension as the sounder position, leaving things without a status that entails reward or punishment.
rows.anchor: وإنما تظهر ثمرة المسألة في حكم الأشياء أيام الفترة قبل النبوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says the pre-prophetic interval need not be framed this way: after revelation, where no text, analogy, or valid inference settles a case, harms are forbidden and benefits permitted, following al-Rāzī's al-Maḥṣūl.
rows.anchor: فإن وجد فعل لم يدل عليه دليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The discourse shifts from the familiar creation of earth to the greater creation of heaven, which people may overlook as evidence of God; the shift expands the reminder of divine power.
rows.anchor: انتقال من الاستدلال بخلق الأرض وما فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When clauses about one subject are joined by thumma, it can mark an imagined delay in rank: the following point is weightier and deserves renewed attention; the author illustrates this with al-Balad and a line by Ṭarafa.
rows.anchor: للمهلة في الرتبة وهي مهلة تخييلية في الأصل تشير إلى أن المعطوف بثم أعرق في المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thumma usually marks rank when clauses report one subject, but real temporal succession when the subjects differ; 2:84–85 and the passing of two armies illustrate chronological order.
rows.anchor: أكثر ما يرد فيما إذا كانت الجمل إخبارا عن مخبر عنه واحد بخلاف ما إذا اختلف المخبر عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If heaven followed earth in creation, thumma marks both temporal and rank delay; if heaven came first, it marks rank alone.
rows.anchor: فأما هذه الآية فإنه إذا كانت السماوات متأخرا خلقها عن خلق الأرض فثم للتراخي الرتبي لا محالة مع التراخي الزمني

rows.speaker: الجمهور ومنهم مجاهد والحسن
rows.claim: Most early authorities, including Mujāhid and al-Ḥasan, with the view also attributed to Ibn ʿAbbās, place earth's creation before heaven, citing this verse and 41:9–11.
rows.anchor: قال الجمهور منهم مجاهد والحسن ونسب إلى ابن عباس إن خلق الأرض متقدم على خلق السماء

rows.speaker: قتادة والسدي ومقاتل
rows.claim: Qatāda, al-Suddī, and Muqātil place heaven's creation before earth, citing the statement that earth was spread after heaven was built.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة والسدي ومقاتل إن خلق السماء متقدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reconciliation is that earth was created first, heaven next, and earth's spreading came afterward; geological accounts describe cooling, crust formation, cracking, sinking, and uplift, though God could bring such change about quickly.
rows.anchor: وقد أجيب بأن الأرض خلقت أولا ثم خلقت السماء ثم دحيت الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author favors heaven before earth: after that in 79:30 states succession more clearly than thumma here, astronomy treats earth as detached from the sun, and Genesis appears to give the same order; Quranic summary avoids the dispute.
rows.anchor: وأرجح القولين هو أن السماء خلقت قبل الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sky may mean the atmosphere surrounding earth, which came after it, or the celestial bodies, which fit the seven heavens and may have preceded earth; Quranic passages may use either sense.
rows.anchor: والسماء إن أريد بها الجو المحيط بالكرة الأرضية فهو تابع لها متأخر عن خلقها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istiwāʾ basically means straightness; figuratively with ilā it means to direct oneself toward something resolutely and quickly, here likening God's decisive will to prepare for a great, exact work.
rows.anchor: ويطلق مجازا على القصد إلى الشيء بعزم وسرعة كأنه يسير إليه مستويا لا يلوي على شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The iftaʿala form is figurative and suggests that heaven and its inhabitants were created among the first things, as preparation for earth and ultimately humanity, the story's focus.
rows.anchor: وفيه إشارة إلى أنه لما ابتدأ خلق المخلوقات خلق السماوات ومن فيها ليكون توطئة لخلق الأرض ثم خلق الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sawwāhun means that God created the heavens in ordered perfection without flaw or defect; istawā and sawwāhun form a modified paronomasia.
rows.anchor: أي خلقهن في استقامة ، واستقامة الخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Samāʾ derives from elevation and can name one upper realm or the class of realms above earth; here it is generic because the verse says it was made seven heavens.
rows.anchor: والسماء مشتقة من السمو وهو العلو واسم السماء يطلق على الواحد وعلى الجنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun hun returns to samāʾ understood generically as a plural; al-Zamakhsharī also allows samāʾ to mean the upper direction, which is possible but unnecessary according to al-Taftāzānī.
rows.anchor: باعتبار إرادة الجنس لأنه في معنى الجمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although God alone knows the seven heavens' full nature, the author considers the likely scientific referent to be the great celestial bodies, the planets in the solar system with earth.
rows.anchor: إلا أن الظاهر الذي دلت عليه القواعد العلمية أن المراد من السماوات الأجرام العلوية العظيمة وهي الكواكب السيارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The declaration of universal knowledge follows from the signs of power: such creation can only issue from one who knows; it also rebukes the ugliness of disbelieving in the all-knowing God.
rows.anchor: نتيجة لما ذكره من دلائل القدرة التي لا تصدر إلا من عليم

rows.speaker: جميع المليين
rows.claim: All religious communities affirm God's universal knowledge, while philosophers deny that He knows particulars; the author dismisses their claim as groundless.
rows.anchor: وقد قال بذلك جميع المليين كما

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read the hāʾ in huwa with ḍamma, the default vocalization.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور هاء ( وهو ) بالضم على الأصل

rows.speaker: قالون وأبو عمرو والكسائي وأبو جعفر
rows.claim: Qālūn, Abū ʿAmr, al-Kisāʾī, and Abū Jaʿfar read the hāʾ in huwa with sukūn to lighten it after a conjunction; this is common Arabic usage, supported by poetic meter.
rows.anchor: وقرأها قالون وأبو عمرو والكسائي وأبو جعفر بالسكون للتخفيف عند دخول حرف العطف عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The waw moves from the creation of heaven and earth to the creation of the first human, combining proofs of oneness and the falsehood of shirk while shifting to earth's human ruler.
rows.anchor: عطفت الواو قصة خلق أول البشر على قصة خلق السماوات والأرض انتقالا بهم في الاستدلال على أن الله واحد وعلى بطلان شركهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mention of creation for humanity prepared listeners for the account of humanity's origin, which displays God's power, favor in creating and privileging humans, and appointing them as stewards.
rows.anchor: تهيأت أنفسهم لسماع قصة إيجاد منشأ الناس الذين خلقت الأرض لأجلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humanity's first creation is the striking beginning of the life that underlies God's creation of earthly things for people, making this transition apt and independently momentous.
rows.anchor: فكان خلق أصلنا هو أبدع مظاهر إحيائنا الذي هو الأصل في خلق ما في الأرض لنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idh is a time noun for a past relation concurrent with another past relation; because its time is vague, it is always annexed to a clarifying clause.
rows.anchor: من أسماء الزمان المبهمة تدل على زمان نسبة ماضية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idh usually functions as an adverbial accusative governed by the verb, but al-Zamakhsharī and Ibn Hishām allow it to function as an object, contrary to the apparent majority view.
rows.anchor: وقد تخرج ( إذ ) عن النصب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In expressions such as yawmaʾidh, idh is added to another time noun in a formal construction, signaling that its normally required clause has been omitted.
rows.anchor: وقد يضاف إليها اسم زمان نحو يومئذ وساعتئذ فتجر بإضافة صورية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One proposed implication of the angels' words is that they claim a stronger title to stewardship: their constant obedience contrasts with the expected corruption of the human appointee.
rows.anchor: الاحتمال الثاني : أن يكون الغرض من قولهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On this reading, the angels' statement is a circumstantial clause governed by tajʿalu, while the implied astonishment and challenge also let the interrogative act as its governing element.
rows.anchor: فتكون حالا مقررة لمدلول جملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tasbīḥ is speech, or speech with action, that magnifies and declares God free of deficiency; hence remembrance and prayer can be called tasbīḥ.
rows.anchor: والتسبيح قول أو مجموع قول مع عمل يدل على تعظيم الله تعالى وتنزيهه

rows.speaker: قوم من أهل اللغة
rows.claim: Some derive tasbīḥ from rapid swimming, extended to the courses of stars and a running horse, and suggest it evokes swift passage in worship.
rows.anchor: وقد ذكروا أن التسبيح مشتق من السبح وهو الذهاب السريع في الماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author considers derivation from swimming by metaphor remote; he prefers derivation from subḥān, with the doubled verb pattern, and notes no un-doubled form meaning glorify is attested.
rows.anchor: وعندي أن كون التسبيح مأخوذا من السبح على وجه المجاز بعيد والوجه أنه مأخوذ من كلمة سبحان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bāʾ marks accompaniment: the angels glorify God with praise, since their utterance includes praise and exaltation, avoiding strained analyses of the phrase.
rows.anchor: فالباء للملابسة أي نسبح تسبيحا مصحوبا بالحمد لك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taqdīs means declaring free of deficiency and purifying; it can be enacted in practice, as the word muqaddas in Imruʾ al-Qays's verse suggests.
rows.anchor: والتقديس التنزيه والتطهير وهو إما بالفعل كما أطلق المقدس على الراهب في قول امرىء القيس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taqdīs may also be an act of belief; the hadith lā quddisat umma means God has not purified a community from satanic impurities when its weak cannot claim rights.
rows.anchor: وإما بالاعتقاد كما في الحديث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although qaddasa is transitive directly, the lām with its object intensifies the action, as in shakarta laka and naṣaḥtu laka; Arabic usage treats this as eloquent emphasis.
rows.anchor: وفعل قدس يتعدى بنفسه فالإتيان باللام مع مفعوله في الآية لإفادة تأكيد حصول الفعل نحو شكرت لك ونصحت لك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects analyses that attach laka to an omitted word or make it mean for your sake with an omitted object, calling these departures from eloquent usage; an explanatory lām remains possible.
rows.anchor: لا تذهب مع الذين جعلوا قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels mean that they exalt God through speech and action and declare Him pure through belief in the perfections fitting the divine essence, so the verbs are not redundant.
rows.anchor: نحن نعظمك وننزهك والأول بالقول والعمل والثاني باعتقاد صفات الكمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nominal sentence marks the angels' enduring disposition; fronting we may suggest exclusive constancy, but the author considers simple emphasis more likely.
rows.anchor: وأوثرت الجملة الاسمية في قوله

words: قَالَ إِنِّىٓ أَعْلَمُ مَا لَا تَعْلَمُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's reply answers the angels' question in the dialogue: He knows the human qualities of both virtue and corruption.
rows.anchor: أي أعلم ما في البشر من صفات الصلاح ومن صفات الفساد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human virtue fulfills the purpose of cultivating earth, while corruption does not erase that purpose; the whole includes major benefits and displays human differences and divine knowledge, will, and power.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن صلاحه يحصل منه المقصد من تعمير الأرض وأن فساده لا يأتي على المقصد بالإبطال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human virtues may emerge from paired defects: courage, for example, lies between recklessness and cowardice.
rows.anchor: ومن أبدع ذلك أن تركب الصفتين الذميمتين يأتي بصفات الفضائل كحدوث الشجاعة من بين طرفي التهور والجبن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording need not add what the angels do know after what they do not know, since that is obvious; the emphasis is on the reach of God's knowledge beyond theirs.
rows.anchor: لا حاجة هنا لتقدير وما تعلمون بعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement closes the exchange and summarizes the proof: God's knowledge exceeds the angels' and He chose Adam as steward knowing his fitness; inna treats their questioning as doubt.
rows.anchor: وتأكيد الجملة بأن لتنزيل الملائكة في مراجعتهم وغفلتهم عن الحكمة منزلة المترددين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning Adam after the dialogue identifies him as the khalīfa and says Adam is the name of that first steward.
rows.anchor: وعطف ذكر آدم بعد ذكر مقالة الله للملائكة وذكر محاورتهم يدل على أن هذا الخليفة هو آدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author calls the sequence a striking movement from general statement to detailed explication and brevity, illustrated by al-Nābigha's poem, whose later lines clarify an earlier allusion.
rows.anchor: كما قال النابغة : فقلت لهم لا أعرفن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adam is the Arabic name of the first human and father of humanity; it may be borrowed from Hebrew adāmā, earth, familiar through the Torah's account and Jewish storytelling.
rows.anchor: وآدم اسم الإنسان الأول أبي البشر في لغة العرب وقيل منقول من العبرانية لأن أداما بالعبرانية بمعنى الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, Arabic and Hebrew may have inherited the name independently from a common Semitic language source.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون هذا الاسم عرف عند العرب والعبرانيين معا من أصل اللغات السامية

rows.speaker: دائرة المعارف العربية
rows.claim: The Arabic Encyclopedia says Adam named himself Īsh, glossed as possessor of acquisition and translated as human or reader; the author suspects Īth was corrupted.
rows.anchor: ووقع في ( دائرة المعارف العربية )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author suggests the encyclopedia's form Īsh may be a corruption of Īth, pointing ahead to the discussion of 2:35.
rows.anchor: قلت ولعله تحريف ( إيث ) كما ستعلمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The following verse's teaching of Adam and demonstration of his distinction give detailed evidence for his fitness as steward, explaining what the angels did not know.
rows.anchor: جعله الله حجة على قوله لهم
